## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Sakkāra Sutta* ("Esteem", Iti 81) is a short discourse in the *Tikanipāta* of the *Itivuttaka* (numbered as It 3.32, PTS It 73) [SuttaCentral]. The sutta warns against the spiritual dangers of letting one's mind become consumed or overwhelmed by whether or not one receives offerings, veneration, and esteem [SuttaCentral].
SuttaCentral identifies curated parallels to this discourse in the *Sagāthakasutta* of the *Lābhasakkāra Saṁyutta* (SN 17.10) and the *Sāriputtattheragāthā* of the *Theragāthā* (Thag 17.2) [SuttaCentral]. Automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus strongly corroborates the link to the *Lābhasakkāra Saṁyutta*, showing extensive passage-level sharing with SN 17.10 (§2.1–5.1 ↔ §10.1.3–10.1.6) [DharmaNexus]. In addition, DharmaNexus detects text reuse across numerous canonical works, including the *Tikanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 3), the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Pārājika 1), neighboring *Itivuttaka* discourses (Iti 70 and Iti 71), and several discourses of the *Majjhima Nikāya* (such as MN 12, MN 41, MN 42, MN 129, MN 130, MN 135, and MN 136) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignment, DharmaNexus notes a match with the Chinese *Yīngwǔ jīng* (鸚鵡經, T 79) [DharmaNexus].
None of the secondary literature passages retrieved in the research corpus discuss Iti 81 directly; the hits merely reflect incidental occurrences of the common Pali term *sakkāra* ("honour", "veneration", or ritual offerings) in general doctrinal formulas, glossaries, or unrelated Southeast Asian liturgical contexts.
